items.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022
items.q: Bill Stapleton, Tony Klatka — these are all fellas that really went right to the band you know, they stayed for a while, and especially Alan Broadbent.

ctx.x: The pre — as I said — pre-Finale, when you can’t hear things back, I think there’s nothing like that first experience — you write a chart, you go to all the trouble, perhaps you copy your own parts, you pass it out and that first time you hear it is rather unforgettable. At least it has been for me.

Well I’ve experienced that by writing the one that Joe Zawinul actually — he played the “Carnavalito” on the synthesizer and I divided it up for the whole band. And that is a thing in which I really appreciated that I was able to really tackle, put it that way. And then of course I wrote “Countdown” of course, another thing which is one of my pride arrangements that I really cherish actually, and also I know Stan Getz, I wrote “Tide Land” for him, and that was another thing which was never really distributed. But…

Yes. Let me take you back. I’m interested in the very start of your musical career. And I believe I read that taking up music was partly a practical thing, a family decision. You were helping make money for the family. Is that correct?
